explanation: Breaststrokers found they went faster by bringing their arms forward over the water. The rules then split the two, and butterfly got its own Olympic races in 1956.

claims.text: Butterfly developed from breaststroke and was recognized as a separate stroke in the 1950s.
Butterfly did not develop from backstroke, front crawl or sidestroke.
In the 1930s some breaststroke swimmers began bringing their arms forward over the water, which was faster.
Butterfly events were first held at the Olympics in 1956.
